extracted.intended_audience: Scientists in the UK at an early career stage or returning from a career break who are considering applying for the Royal Society Research Grants scheme
extracted.subtask_description: Applying for the Royal Society Research Grants scheme (seed-corn funding up to £30,000 for up to 12 months) aimed at newly independent researchers or those returning from career breaks, including preparing eligibility evidence, proposal, abstract and requested budget items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme objectives — enable preliminary data and strengthen future funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable newly independent researchers to gather preliminary data, develop their research ideas and strengthen applications for further funding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheme provides ‘seed corn’ funding for up to 12 months for independent researchers; proposals should therefore be aimed at producing preliminary data or developing ideas that will make future, larger funding applications more competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme objectives — support returners from career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Support independent researchers returning to academia after a career break to enable them to develop new ideas and research questions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants returning from a career break should frame proposals to re-establish research momentum and develop new directions; the scheme explicitly aims to enable this transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme objectives — increase availability of equipment and consumables
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the availability of equipment and consumables for researchers at the beginning of their career and those returning from career breaks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding is targeted at tangible resources (equipment, consumables) that enable early-stage research activity; applicants should justify requests for such items as essential to achieving the proposal objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme provides up to £30,000 of funding for up to 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and project duration must fit within these caps; full funding details and allowable cost categories are provided in the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can cover: equipment; consumables; travel costs and subsistence for essential field research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should only budget for these categories unless otherwise specified in the scheme notes; justification for travel/subsistence must show it is essential for the field research component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — doctoral qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: You hold a PhD or equivalent qualification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate an appropriate doctoral-level qualification or equivalent experience as described in the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — career stage (first five years of independent research post)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are within the first five years of an independent research post, at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be your first permanent independent academic research post, your first independent research fellowship or a named limited-tenured/fixed-term academic research post, obtained in open competition. Read Annex 1 for examples of eligible career positions and for guidance on counting eligibility time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — tenure must cover award duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenure must cover the duration of the award
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your post is limited term, the appointment must at minimum cover the 12-month award period; ensure institutional support and appointment dates align with the award duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — UK organisation and residency
rubrics_metrics.description: You are based at an eligible UK organisation and a UK resident at the time of application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be hosted by eligible UK institutions and resident in the UK when applying; consult scheme notes for list of eligible organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — fully independent researcher status
rubrics_metrics.description: You are a fully independent researcher with access to your own lab space and with the ability to recruit and be registered as the primary supervisor of PhD students and research assistants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate independence (lab space, supervisory authority and ability to recruit); this distinguishes candidates from those in mentored or non-independent positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — research within Royal Society remit
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research is within the Royal Society’s remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm subject area by consulting the Royal Society's breakdown of subject groups and areas supported; a new question in the application now asks for the primary subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content — scientific abstract required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are now required to submit a scientific abstract in addition to the lay summary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare both a technical abstract for scientific reviewers and an accessible lay summary; follow any length/format guidance in the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission system
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply through our application and grant management system, Flexi-Grant®
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and submit via Flexi-Grant; consult the 'Application and assessment process' page and scheme notes for system-specific instructions and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment procedure — panel review and shortlisting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of your application will be overseen by the Royal Society Research Grants panel. Following eligibility checks, applications are initially reviewed and assessed by a minimum of two panel members who have the most appropriate scientific expertise. Following completion of the panel assessment, a shortlist is drawn up. Shortlisted applications are reviewed by the Panel Chair and the recommendations for funding are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are peer-reviewed by panel members with relevant expertise (minimum two reviewers); expect shortlisting and an additional review by the Chair. Emphasise scientific quality and fit to scheme objectives to appeal to expert reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for delivering excellence in STEM and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences to maximise innovation and creativity in science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Society reviews and revises policies and processes to embed EDI principles into grant making and ensure all talented applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per assessment criteria; applicants may reference EDI-relevant aspects of their work/career where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and adjustments for disabled applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society provides support and adjustments to ensure disabled applicants can participate fully in the selection process; requests are treated in confidence and not normally shared with panel members unless relevant to assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available adjustments include: extension of the deadline; additional support to complete the application form; receiving the application form in a different format (e.g., Word document); support during interviews including technical support for accessibility software/services; and additional costs that candidates may incur to attend an interview because of their disability. Contact researchgrants@royalsociety.org to request adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and supplementary documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should read the scheme notes and related documents (Research Grants scheme notes 2026, Conditions of Award, FAQs) for full details on eligibility, allowable costs and the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page indicates updated guidance has been included in the scheme notes to support writing the research proposal and that Annex 1 contains examples of eligible career positions; applicants must consult these documents for detailed formatting, scoring criteria and procedural requirements.
